story.title: Tragic Capsizing of Migrant Boat off Djibouti Leaves 139 Dead and 84 Missing
story.summary: A migrant boat capsized off the coast of Djibouti, resulting in at least 139 confirmed deaths, including 15 children. The International Organization for Migration reported that 84 individuals remain missing, while 82 survivors, all Ethiopian nationals, have been accounted for. The vessel was reportedly carrying over 300 people en route to Yemen when the incident occurred.

explore_lenses.label: What do survivor accounts say went wrong?
explore_lenses.title: Overcrowding and a rapid capsize
explore_lenses.summary: Survivor accounts cited by IOM indicate the vessel capsized near Guhere, north of Obock, during the night of October 8–9. Reporting describes a boat carrying 305 people that began sinking from the rear shortly after passengers boarded.

claims.text: IOM, citing survivors, placed the capsize near Guhere north of Obock and said it occurred between the night of October 8 and before dawn on October 9.

IOM’s Djibouti chief, Alexandre Coissac, told AFP the boat carried 305 people and was far too small for that number; he said survivors reported that it started sinking from the rear as soon as they boarded.

explore_lenses.label: Why do migrants still take this route?
explore_lenses.title: A continuing route toward Gulf work
explore_lenses.summary: The voyage is part of the Eastern Route linking the Horn of Africa to Yemen and, for many migrants, onward to Gulf labour markets. IOM says the traffic has continued despite conflict in Yemen and severe risks in Djibouti.

claims.text: IOM said it recorded more than 20,000 incoming migrant movements from Ethiopia to Djibouti between September 10 and October 6, while 539 Ethiopian migrants returned from Yemen in the same period.

Coissac said migrants remained focused on reaching Gulf countries for a better life; AFP reported that roughly 150 people aboard had previously been returned from Yemen and attempted the crossing again.
IOM’s director general, Amy Pope, argued that governments and donors should expand safe, legal migration channels, framing them as a life-saving alternative to dangerous irregular crossings.

explore_lenses.label: What aid and operations are confirmed now?
explore_lenses.title: Rescue work and survivor support continue
explore_lenses.summary: Djiboutian authorities were continuing search-and-rescue activity while IOM said it was working alongside them on emergency assistance. The response also includes immediate health, shelter and family-contact support for survivors.

claims.text: Search-and-rescue operations were continuing after the capsize, according to IOM and reporting based on its statements.
IOM said its teams were providing emergency assistance with local authorities; Africanews reported healthcare and help contacting relatives for survivors.
AFP reported that IOM was assisting 64 survivors at its Obock migrant-response center with healthcare, temporary accommodation and food, while Djiboutian authorities conducted searches.

story_report.summary: A migrant boat carrying more than 300 people capsized off Djibouti, leaving 139 people confirmed dead, including 15 children, and 84 missing. Eighty-two survivors, all Ethiopians, have been accounted for. The International Organization for Migration said the disaster occurred near Guhere, north of Obock, between the night of October 8 and before dawn on October 9; search-and-rescue operations were continuing.

sections.heading: Survivor Accounts of the Capsize
sections.body: IOM’s Djibouti chief, Alexandre Coissac, told AFP that the vessel carried 305 people and was far too small for that number. He said survivors reported that the boat began sinking from the rear as soon as passengers boarded. Those accounts describe the circumstances reported by survivors, rather than establishing a final technical explanation for the sinking.

sections.heading: Migration Route Through Djibouti
sections.body: IOM recorded more than 20,000 incoming migrant movements from Ethiopia to Djibouti between September 10 and October 6, while 539 Ethiopian migrants returned from Yemen during the same period. Coissac said migrants remained focused on reaching Gulf countries in search of a better life. AFP reported that about 150 people aboard the capsized boat had previously been returned from Yemen and attempted the crossing again.

sections.heading: Searches and Survivor Assistance
sections.body: IOM said it was providing emergency assistance alongside local authorities as searches continued. AFP reported that IOM was assisting 64 survivors at its Obock migrant-response center with healthcare, temporary accommodation and food, while Djiboutian authorities conducted searches. Other reporting said survivors were receiving healthcare and help contacting relatives.

unresolved.text: Available accounts do not establish the final technical cause of the capsize, whether the vessel suffered a mechanical failure, or who arranged the crossing.
No confirmed timetable was available for ending the search, identifying all victims, or recovering the missing people.

related_stories.title: Trump Criticizes Zelenskyy, Suggests Ukraine Needs New Leadership
related_stories.summary: Donald Trump has criticized Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, suggesting that Ukraine should elect a new president. He blamed Zelenskyy for rising US diesel prices and criticized his failure to negotiate a peace deal with Russia. Trump also cautioned Ukraine against targeting Russian oil refineries that supply diesel fuel to the US.

related_stories.title: Trump Announces Energy Ceasefire Between Russia and Ukraine
related_stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to an 'energy ceasefire' amid ongoing tensions. However, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed skepticism, stating that this was 'news for me' and indicated that Ukraine would halt strikes on Russian oil refineries only if Russia ceased its attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Trump's comments have drawn criticism, particularly regarding his previous remarks about Ukraine's leadership.

related_stories.title: Spanish Police Clear Last Migrant Camp in Ceuta Before Royal Visit
related_stories.summary: Spanish police have dismantled the last migrant beach camp in Ceuta, transporting individuals to reception centers for processing. This action took place ahead of a planned visit by the king. Some migrants have reported allegations of mistreatment by Spanish soldiers during the camp clearance.
